answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can vote on job allocations, with one vote per bonded identity. Whether an agent calls itself quartz, ledge, or zephyr, it faces the same deposit rule. Creating 1,000 voting identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, making influence costly in capital and lost liquidity even though generating names and keys is cheap.
